case_name: Sh. Yashpal Chaudhrani & Ors. vs State (Govt. Of Nct Delhi) & Anr.
facts_of_case: Petitioners seek quashing of criminal proceedings on account of 'settlement' of the dispute with the party perceived to be the victim.

legal_principles.principle: The court's inherent power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. can be availed to quash criminal proceedings in serious or heinous crimes.
legal_principles.held: Court which would inhibit the inherent power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to be availed to quash such criminal proceedings in serious or heinous crimes including those reflecting 'mental depravity', as indeed, economic offenses involving 'financial well-being of the State' or financial or banking institutions, affecting the public at large by 'financial or economic fraud(s)'
cited_cases: Sh. Yashpal Chaudhrani & Ors. vs State (Govt. Of Nct Delhi) & Anr., (2019)
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significant in serious or heinous crimes

legal_principles.principle: The court should not entertain matters of a sensitive nature, such as sexual assault, unnatural offence and rape, without proper investigation.
legal_principles.held: But, it was conceded that the allegations of sexual assault, unnatural offence and rape were directed against persons other than the husband.
cited_cases: Sh. Yashpal Chaudhrani & Ors. vs State (Govt. Of Nct Delhi) & Anr., (2019)
use_in: case type 1: criminal cases involving sensitive issues
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — relevant in cases involving sensitive issues

outcome.final_order: The court allows the petition and quashes the criminal proceedings.
